subject: CrestWave: throughput spike — exec war-room & stakeholder updates
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Alex Torres <alex.torres@crestwave.ai>, monica.patel@redwood.com, david.kim@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 10 Oct 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: CrestWave - urgent: throughput spike impacting production routes

Alex / CrestWave team —

Quick heads-up: starting ~07:40 PDT we observed a sharp throughput spike on your v2 inference routes (route ids: cw-v2-gen-*, cw-v2-chat-*). Token throughput is ~5x baseline, p50 latency has risen from ~120ms to ~900ms, and 5xx error rate spiked to ~4.8% (from ~0.1%). Customer-facing traffic is degraded for a subset of tenants.

Immediate asks:
- We're standing up an exec war-room in 15 minutes to triage and assign actions (invite below). Please confirm if your team is already applying any mitigations (rate-limit, fallback routing).
- If possible, please share any recent config deploys, traffic pattern changes, or feature flags toggled in the last 2 hours.
- We've attached an initial incident summary (initial_incident_summary.pdf) with current metrics and trace samples.

Proposed first steps (we're starting these now):
1) Scale additional dedicated inference workers for cw-v2 routes (temporary burst).
2) Route non-critical queries to a lower-capacity model variant (v2-lite) to preserve p95 for transactional requests.
3) Enable aggressive prefix caching for the affected customer prefixes.
4) Collect full KV cache and recent kernel logs for postmortem.

Executive invites: Monica (CS lead), David (SRE lead), Karthik (Infra), Lauren (Head of Support).

I will coordinate the war-room and keep you updated every 30 minutes.

—Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
mateo.alvarez@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachment: initial_incident_summary.pdf
From: Alex Torres <alex.torres@crestwave.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com, david.kim@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 10 Oct 2026 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CrestWave - urgent: throughput spike impacting production routes

Thanks Mateo — appreciate the quick flag.

We're seeing widespread slowdowns on customer-facing endpoints; internal dashboards show retry storms from our gateway starting ~07:30. We temporarily enabled a 20% sample-based rate limit and rolled back a feature flag that increased batch aggregation for the v2 path at 07:35. That reduced immediate request amplification but didn't fully stop elevated latency.

We have two high-impact customers on this path (AcmeHealth and Trendline) who are escalating to our ops leads. We would like a clear timeline for mitigation and whether Redwood can provide a temporary routing rule to divert critical traffic to the v2-lite variant.

Also: will request an SLA credit if the degradation persists >3 hours — want to flag that now.

Alex
Alex Torres
Head of Platform, CrestWave
alex.torres@crestwave.ai

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: mateo.alvarez@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 10 Oct 2026 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: RE: CrestWave - quick technical readout (war-room)

Team — joining war-room now. Initial triage notes:
- Root-cause candidate: a cache invalidation loop triggered by a recent config that inadvertently cleared prefix caches on a hot keyspace (seen in kernel logs at 07:36). This caused increased repeated upstream work and KV cache misses.
- Immediate mitigations under way: scale dedicated pool + warm instances on new nodes; revert the cache invalidation change via hotfix in the control plane (patch attached: runbook_patch.diff).
- Traffic shaping: implementing a temporary routing rule to send 30% of non-auth traffic to v2-lite and 100% of payments/txn traffic to priority lanes.
- ETA: 60–90 minutes for p95 recovery if scale + hotfix succeed; monitoring for error-rate decay.

I'll post metrics snapshots in 10 minutes (metrics_snapshot.png). If the hotfix is problematic we'll fallback to circuit-breaker for affected shard ranges.

—David
David Kim
Director, Site Reliability Engineering
david.kim@redwood.com

Attachment: runbook_patch.diff, metrics_snapshot.png
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: monica.patel@redwood.com, alex.torres@crestwave.ai
Cc: mateo.alvarez@redwood.com, david.kim@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 10 Oct 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: CrestWave — stakeholder communication and next steps (draft)

Monica / Alex —

Summary (for execs and customer comms):
- What happened: an unintended cache invalidation triggered a cascade of KV misses at ~07:36 PDT, amplifying work and spiking throughput for v2 routes.
- What we did: scaled dedicated capacity, applied a targeted hotfix to disable the invalidation, and temporarily routed lower-priority traffic to v2-lite to restore p95 latency for transactional flows.
- Current status: system stable for priority lanes; overall p95 reduced from ~900ms to ~220ms. Error rate trending down (from 4.8% to 0.9%). We continue to monitor.
- Customer impacts: partial degradation for non-critical background workloads; transactional traffic restored to acceptable SLOs. Affected customers: AcmeHealth, Trendline (we've notified both).
- Next steps:
  1) Complete postmortem and share within 48 hours (owner: David K.).
  2) Permanent fix timeline: configuration validation and test harnesses to prevent cache-invalidation regressions (owner: Karthik, ETA 2 weeks).
  3) Compensation request: CrestWave indicated potential SLA credit if >3 hours — we will review and respond via Customer Success + Legal.
  4) Customer comms: Monica to send a customer-facing note; below is a draft.

DRAFT customer-facing note (please comment before I send):

Subject: Update on this morning's performance degradation

Hi Alex —

Thank you for your patience while we investigated the degradation this morning. Root cause analysis indicates a configuration change that caused repeated cache invalidations on a high-volume keyspace, resulting in increased upstream work and elevated latency for non-priority queries.

Our engineers applied a targeted hotfix and routing adjustments that restored transactional traffic to expected latency profiles. We continue to monitor closely and will share a detailed postmortem within 48 hours.

If you'd like a live run-through with our engineering leads, we can schedule a 30-minute review at your convenience.

Regards,
